newsitem.title: DUBAI: First UAE equity fund suspends sales to foreigners.
newsitem.headline: First UAE equity fund suspends sales to foreigners.

text.p: The UAE's first mutual fund has suspended sale of its units to foreigners pending a decision by the UAE Central Bank on the ceiling for foreign participation, an Emirates Bank International (EBI) official said on Monday.
EBI are the managers for the Emirates Equity Fund.
"Subscription by non-UAE nationals exceeded the 20 percent limit allowed by the Central Bank...Suspension is temporary until we receive authorisation to lift this ceiling," he said.
"In the absence of Central Bank authorisation to lift the ceiling, the fund cannot be re-opened to non-nationals unless there is a marked increase in national participation," the EBI official said.

EBI chief executive Anis al-Jallaf said last week the bank had asked the Central Bank to raise the limit for foreign participation to 49 percent from 20 percent. He said at the time that foreigners' subscriptions accounted for some 23 percent.
The open-ended fund attracted subscriptions of about 250 million dirhams ($68 million) compared to the 30 million dirhams fund managers expected to raise.

Analysts said many cash-rich UAE nationals did not see the need to invest in a mutual fund when they could buy a range of shares on the fledgling market. "Buying through an equity fund does not appeal to nationals, they can buy and sell on the open market and reap capital profits and higher returns," said one.
In the past year, the market which BE says is capitalised at 67 billion dirhams, has risen by some 30 percent.
Some 75 percent of the 2.4 million population are foreigners who have so far been excluded from the UAE's informal market.

Central Bank Governor Sultan Nasser al-Suweidi said in an interview in the al-Eqtisadi business weekly that equity funds fall under UAE company law which allows 49 percent foreign ownership. This has prompted analysts to say that a raising of the fund's ceiling for foreigners is now likely.
